title: Cybersecurity stocks surge on mounting AI doomsday fears
excerpt: Markets have been jolted by the abrupt vibe shift in the AI story, but cybersecurity stocks are one corner of tech getting a boost from doomsday fears.
content_html:
Cybersecurity is one corner of the tech market that's getting a boost from AI doomsday fears

By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The AI doomsday conversation has rattled the market, but investors are piling into one corner of tech as worries rise about a future marked by AI-enabled cyberattacks.

Wall Street has been jolted by the abrupt vibe shift in the AI story in recent days. After years of a blistering arms race among the biggest tech companies, AI makers say it's time to slow down, lest humanity be threatened by the growing power of its own creation.

Wall Street fled some of the highest-flying AI stocks, particularly chips, which saw the brunt of Monday's selling. Nvidia, AMD and Intel tumbled. Memory makers like Micron Technology and Korea's SK Hynix saw even steeper declines on the rising fears of an AI apocalypse.

One bright spot amid the tech selling, however, was cybersecurity, which is benefitting from predictions of a future where AI greatly boosts the capabilities of hackers, or even goes rogue and executes its own cyber attacks.

"One thing everyone knows is cyber security will be the biggest benefactor from this AI boom," said Eddie Ghabour, CEO of Key Advisors Wealth Management. "It's the next phase of the market for AI stocks. The more and more AI is adopted, the higher need for cybersecurity."

Here were some of the top gainers in the sector on Monday as of close of markets:

  • Crowdstrike: +14%
  • Zscaler: +16%
  • Palo Alto Networks: +13%
  • SentinelOne: +14%
  • Fortinet: +9%
  • Cloudflare: +8%

A post from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on the Claude maker's website pointed to cyberattacks as a reason behind his call to slow AI development.

"They include the risk of losing control of AI systems, misuse of AI for cyberattacks and bioterrorism, and serious economic disruption," he wrote. "A race to the bottom, spurred by commercial incentives, can make these risks more acute."

The scenario feared by some AI researchers has already played out this year. In July, OpenAI models broke out of their containment and hacked systems at tech startup Hugging Face. Since then, warnings have piled up, with worries about an AI crisis hitting a boiling point last week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned over concerns that frontier labs are not taking the threat seriously.

While confidence in the AI trade is waning, investors are rushing to pile into cybersecurity stocks amid bullish speculation of what the next chapter of the AI story might entail. Citrini Research, which firm went viral for sharing its own AI doomsday scenario early this year, recently predicted that AI would lead to a surge in demand for cybersecurity software.

Chris Versace, senior portfolio manager at TheStreet Pro, told Business Insider that it stands to reason that fear of protecting assets from the growing capabilities of AI is on the rise following the OpenAI Hugging Face hack. The Wall Street Journal reported over the weekend that OpenAI agents also hacked another site earlier in the year before the Hugging Face incident.

"We've been bullish on cybersecurity stocks for a few reasons," Versace said. "Including the need to protect our increasingly connected digital world, but also that AI adoption by bad actors will accelerate the vector and velocity of cyber attacks. We are seeing both."
